findings.location: design.md D5, 'The variables' table and change 1 (`instrument.ts`), against format.ts:190-195 and statusline/spec.md:1130-1133
findings.finding: D5 declares `$tokens`, `$cost`, `$idle`, `$blocks` and `$notice` on the `notice` declaration. The existing `resolveFormat` iterates `declaration.variables` and returns `""` the moment any declared variable resolves `undefined`, and the living spec requires exactly that ('the store reads one of its declared data as unknown → the cell renders nothing, whatever the format is'). D1 says a value the kind does not carry is absent from `values`. So every compaction, branch-summary and thinking notice — and every miss, which carries no `blocks` — renders nothing, label included, even with the default `$notice` format. The premise does not run. The design is also silent on how the binding 'hands that text to the cell's format as the value of composed.variable' when resolvers only receive `Readings`.
findings.required_change: State the variable contract so it runs: `declaration.variables` carries only `notice`; the four value variables are declared on `composed` (e.g. `composed.variables: Record<string, (readings) => string | undefined>`), the plain parse mode validates a kind's format against that set (and rejects `$notice` there), and the binding supplies the composed text as the `notice` value — name the seam (a `resolveFormat` parameter for pre-resolved values, or the binding wrapping the declaration's `notice` resolver). Say what a value absent from `values` renders in a kind's format (`""`, since only the notice is unknown). Then re-check the delta spec's 'A notice's text is a format with declared variables' wording still fits.

findings.location: design.md D3, last two paragraphs; specs/session-data-store/spec.md 'The store's visible time comes from the composition root', scenario 'A rejected document'
findings.finding: D3 defines `noticeSeconds` as `undefined` whenever no installed row places a `notice` cell, and `undefined` means no subscription, no scan record, no timer. A rejected document installs the default row, which places none, so the store receives `undefined`. D3 then says 'the store still holds the declared default visible time for a notice it will never see', and the spec requires 'a document the configuration rejects MUST still leave the store the declared default visible time' with a scenario asserting expiry by it. The two statements contradict, and the scenario is unobservable: no notice can arrive. Deletion test: nothing breaks if the clause goes. D3 also never says how the reader knows a cell is `notice` — `Cell` holds a nameless bound `Instrument` (configuration.ts:139-176, instrument.ts:9-12).
findings.required_change: Remove the spec clause and the 'A rejected document' scenario, or restate them as 'a rejected document installs the default row, which places no notice cell, so the gate is off' under the gating requirement; strike D3's sentence that the store 'still holds the declared default'. Add to D3 how placement is detected (compare the resolved declaration to the imported `notice` declaration in `cellsFromNames`, counting only cells inside the ceiling, or carry the declaration name on `Cell`) and where the default seconds constant is imported from.

findings.location: design.md D1, 'Flow' → `message_end`, and the thinking-drop delta in `data/notice.ts`; against interactive-mode.js:3338-3346 and spec 'A dropped-thinking notice shows only when its count rises'
findings.finding: pi derives the previous count from `this.sessionManager.getBranch()` — the branch's last assistant message — while pi's miss scan reads `getEntries()` (IM:3362). The store's only entry reader is `readEntries: () => ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()`. The design states the delta rule but not which host read supplies the previous assistant message; from `getEntries()` the last assistant message may sit on an abandoned branch after `/tree` navigation, so the notice fires when pi's would not, or stays silent when pi's fires. The D8 boundary test ('count rising vs repeating') feeds the module a previous count and cannot catch the wrong source.
findings.required_change: Name the read: the feed supplies `readBranch: () => ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()` (on `ReadonlySessionManager`, session-manager.d.ts:178, verified) beside `readEntries`, and the `message_end` handler passes the branch to the thinking-drop step while the miss step keeps `getEntries()`, as pi does. Add the input that makes the two sources differ (an assistant message on a sibling branch with a higher count) to D8.

findings.location: design.md D2, 'Two readers, because they do two jobs' and 'A timer that fires early, late or twice cannot extend or shorten a notice'
findings.finding: With the clock deciding and the timer only repainting, a callback that runs while `now() < deadline` leaves the notice showing with no further repaint scheduled until the host renders for its own reasons — the failure D2 rejects the lazy-drop alternative for. I measured 1,000 `setTimeout` trials on Node 26 and none fired before `Date.now() >= deadline`, so the timer is not the exposure; `Date.now` is: it is wall-clock and steps (sleep/NTP), and `performance.now()` is monotonic at the same cost.
findings.required_change: Name the root's clock as `performance.now` (monotonic) rather than `Date.now`, and state the early-fire consequence honestly in D2, or have the callback re-arm for `deadline - now()` when it finds the deadline not yet reached. Documentation-plus-one-identifier change; Derek can carry it under D2.
